purpose: Select one tokenizer prospectively using tokenizer-intrinsic Korean criteria, then freeze it across S0-S3 so model-capacity effects are not confounded with tokenization.

candidates.rationale: Strong baseline with no lexical OOV; historically common in Korean GPT-style models.
Frequency-based subword baseline with flexible segmentation and compact vocabulary.
2026 Korean evidence suggests morphology-aware segmentation can reduce token count and improve downstream performance; included as a rival, not presumed winner.

court_design.tokenizer_training_text: A fixed tokenizer-only slice from the P50 training-authorized corpus; no PIA/evaluation text.
court_design.selection_rule: Pareto court; no single weighted scalar. Reject any tokenizer with nonzero unrecoverable OOV or severe Hangul/Jamo fragmentation. Among survivors, choose a non-dominated tokenizer before any SLM PIA result exists.

capacity_firewall: The tokenizer winner and vocabulary size are identical for S0-S3.
Tokenizer embeddings are reported separately from non-embedding transformer parameters.
No tokenizer retuning after seeing PIA or governance outcomes.
If T2 requires a morphological analyzer, analyzer version and failure policy are frozen and its errors do not gain semantic authority.
evidence_context: KoGPT2 historically used Korean-trained BPE/Character-BPE vocabularies around 50k.
EACL 2026 reports advantages for morpheme-based Korean subword tokenization, motivating T2 as a live rival.
